designNotes: Local MCP HTTP broker only: node:http on 127.0.0.1:random, POST /mcp JSON-RPC 2.0, JSON bodies, no SSE/sampling/resources/approval. Host must be exact 127.0.0.1:bound-port; any Origin is forbidden; Bearer is timing-safe and checked before the body is read.

Exactly one tool, memory_propose. Metadata states proposal only, the tool does not change memory, human review is MEMORY_PROPOSAL_REVIEW_LOCATION, and uncertain replies retry SAME requestId + payload. inputSchema is a closed discriminated union for add/replace/remove/batch; batch operations cannot nest target or batch; no aliases, digest fields, or approval tool.

Transport RPC id (type-tagged n: vs s:) is distinct from input.requestId. Cache key is RPC id plus SHA-256 of the raw body, not proposal text. Same id+body shares one in-flight promise; same id+different body is conflict; a new RPC id with the same requestId+payload always reaches propose. Native host remains the durable idempotency authority.

tools/call is gated on isActive plus assertCapability('reasoning') (default managedService.assertCapability('reasoning')) before dispatch, after propose returns, and immediately before any success reply including cache replay. initialize/tools/list/ping are allowed while inactive. Notifications cannot call the tool.

cancelPending increments generation and aborts tracked controllers. In-flight work that later settles is stored as uncertain so a new turn cannot adopt an old callback result or redispatch that RPC id. Completed success is retained and replayed only when the current gate permits.

HTTP is released by racing propose against abort, 35s timeout, and disconnect. Live callback accounting (max 4) stays until propose actually settles; unhandled rejections are suppressed. close revokes the bearer, aborts work, and closes/destroys the server so responses cannot hang. Errors are a fixed string set with no provider/argument/path/identity/exception data.
testCases: Binds 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port and returns descriptor {type:'http',name:'memory-proposals',url:http://127.0.0.1:port/mcp,headers:[{name:'authorization',value:'Bearer <64-hex>'}]}.

POST /mcp with Host 127.0.0.1:port and valid Bearer: initialize returns protocolVersion 2024-11-05, capabilities.tools {}, and serverInfo; tools/list returns only memory_propose with proposal-only title/description, exact review location, SAME requestId + payload retry text, and additionalProperties:false discriminated add/replace/remove/batch schemas without nested target/batch, aliases, or digest/approval fields; ping returns {}; notifications/initialized without id returns 202.

Discovery (initialize/tools/list/ping) succeeds while isActive is false; tools/call while inactive returns inactive and does not call propose; assertCapability throw returns unavailable and does not call propose.

Reject ANY Origin, wrong Host (localhost, IPv6, missing port), missing/wrong Authorization, GET, and non-/mcp path without reading a large body; bound body >70KiB is 413; malformed UTF-8 is 400 invalid encoding; body read longer than 10s is 408.

JSON-RPC id must be a safe integer or nonempty string length<=100 without controls; number 1 and string '1' are distinct cache keys; tools/call without id does not dispatch; unknown keys on the envelope or tools/call params, nested batch, extra payload keys, and unknown tool names are invalid request/params with fixed strings.

Valid add/replace/remove/batch call returns only {version:1,id:/^[a-f0-9]{8}$/,reviewLocation:fixed} as both text content JSON and structuredContent; propose extra fields are stripped; propose throw, invalid result, or abort-ignored late success after cancelPending become uncertain with no leaked exception/path/argument data.

Concurrent tools/call with the same RPC id and body share one propose; same RPC id with a different body is conflict and does not dispatch; a new RPC id with the same requestId+payload calls propose again; after uncertain/error for an RPC id, a later same id+body replays the fixed uncertain/error and does not redispatch.

cancelPending aborts in-flight HTTP promptly, increments generation, and prevents a later turn from adopting the old callback success on that RPC id without clearing history into a redispatch; cached success still replays only when currently active and reasoning-capable.

Fifth concurrent propose is busy; a callback that ignores abort still counts until settlement; HTTP timeout at 35s returns timeout without waiting for the ignored abort; client disconnect neither writes success nor leaks; close revokes the token (subsequent Bearer 401), aborts work, and does not leave the HTTP server hanging.
